title: MA8-09260
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, the claimant, is a citizen of Mexico. She is claiming refugee protection in Canada under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA). In support of her claim, she alleged the following.

The claimant alleged that she fears that she will be killed in her country by one XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, who stole cheques that she had in her possession and cashed them at the HSBC bank, according to her inquiries with the bank. Since she discovered that Mr. XXXXX XXXXX stole these cheques, she has been threatened, forcibly confined and seriously assaulted.

Alleging that she feared for her life after the assault on XXXXX, 2007, the claimant stated that she went to hide at her aunt's home, where she made the decision to leave Mexico. She left her country on XXXXX 2007, to come to Canada. She arrived in Montréal the same day and claimed refugee protection at the airport.

Having heard your testimony and having examined all of the evidence on file, I determine that your claim for refugee protection cannot be allowed. I have made this determination for the following reasons.

On the basis of your testimony and the evidence on file, I determine that there is no nexus to a Convention ground. It is also not a case of torture, and therefore paragraph 97(1)(a) does not apply because there is no involvement of any public official or other person acting for or with the consent of a public official. Consequently, I will analyze this claim under paragraph 97(1)(b) of the IRPA. Identity
I am satisfied as to your identity. It was established by means of your passport, which was seized by Citizenship and Immigration Canada. Credibility

Your testimony was emotional and candid, and you gave direct answers to all the questions you were asked. I noted no omissions or contradictions between your testimony, the Personal Information Form (PIF) and the port-of-entry interview notes. Therefore, I find that your testimony was credible. Internal flight alternative (IFA)

First, I had to determine whether there exists a serious possibility that you will be persecuted or exposed, on a balance of probabilities, to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment in the region of Veracruz. Second, I had to assess whether it would be objectively unreasonable for you to seek refuge in the region of Veracruz.

Initially, I asked you whether, after everything that you went through, you thought about relocating elsewhere. You responded: [translation] "I felt bad; I was trapped in my problems. My life had changed; I could not go out or sleep in peace". Shortly after, following a question from your lawyer, I asked you how, if you moved 800 km away from his home, Mr. XXXXX could find you and assault you again. You told me that he has access to all the documents, that he is in the government and, consequently, he could find you. I then referred you to the National Documentation Package on Mexico,1 which states that a court order is required to gain access to Mexicans' personal information. Consequently, I reject your explanation that he could find you anywhere in Mexico, and in particular, in Veracruz, by using the personal information databases.

Given your testimony and the documentary evidence, I consider that you did not demonstrate that, in all of Mexico, there is a real risk to your life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment. In this case, I am of the opinion that you did not meet the burden of proving that your life would be in danger in Veracruz. I conclude that you did not establish that you would be exposed to a risk to your life if you were to settle in Veracruz.

Second, I asked you whether, if you did not have problems with this member of your party, given your work experience and your training, you could find a job and make your living in Veracruz. You said yes, that without these problems, you could find a job. Then I asked you, while giving you examples, whether, in your opinion, there would be obstacles preventing you from relocating to Veracruz, if you did not have the problems with the member of your party. You told me again: [translation] "because of the fear of what I experienced". These explanations do not answer the question and do not indicate that other obstacles exist to prevent you from relocating to Veracruz. You did not suggest other obstacles that would render the region of Veracruz unreasonable.

In light of your testimony, I am of the opinion that you did not satisfy me that, on a balance of probabilities, you would be at risk in Veracruz and that, given all of the circumstances, including your own, the situation in Mexico is such that it is unreasonable for you to seek refuge there.
In this case, I consider that Veracruz is a reasonable IFA for you.

Consequently, based on your testimony, the documentation on Mexico and the exhibits on file, I conclude that, because the existence of an IFA means that you would not be subjected to a risk in every part of that country, as required by paragraph 97(1)(b), and because you did not demonstrate that the Veracruz option was unreasonable, you are not a "person in need of protection".

Having considered all the evidence, I conclude that you did not demonstrate, on a balance of probabilities, that upon your return to Mexico, you would be personally subjected to a danger of torture or to a risk to your life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

For all these reasons, I determine that XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX is not a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA or a "person in need of protection" under paragraphs 97(1)(a) and (b) of the said Act.

Consequently, the refugee protection claim is rejected.
